title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY AND WORK-FAMILY BALANCE ASSISTANCE ACT
title_original: 남녀고용평등과 일ㆍ가정 양립 지원에 관한 법률 시행령
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters mandated by the Equal Employment Opportunity and Work-Family Balance Assistance Act and matters necessary for the enforcement thereof.

Article 2 (Scope of application) (1) Under the proviso of Article 3 (1) of the Equal Employment Opportunity and Work-Family Balance Assistance Act (hereinafter referred to as the “Act”), the whole of the Act shall not apply to a business or workplace consisting of only relatives living together (hereinafter referred to as “business”) or to housekeeping employees.
  (2) Deleted. <May 28, 2018>

CHAPTER II GUARANTEE OF EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES AND TREATMENT IN EMPLOYMENT OF MEN AND WOMEN

Article 3 (Workplace sexual harassment prevention education) (1) An employer shall provide workplace sexual harassment prevention education under Article 13 of the Act at least once a year.
  (2) The prevention education under paragraph (1) shall include the following matters:
  1. Statutes or regulations relating to workplace sexual harassment;
  2. Handling procedures and standards for measures upon the occurrence of workplace sexual harassment at the relevant workplace;
  3. Grievance counseling and remedial procedures for harassed employees relating to workplace sexual harassment at the relevant workplace;
  4. Other matters necessary for the prevention of workplace sexual harassment.
  (3) The prevention education under paragraph (1) may be provided, in consideration of the size, characteristics, etc. of the business, through employee training, staff assemblies, meetings, or cyber education using an information and communications network such as the Internet; provided, where it is impracticable to verify whether the educational content has been properly delivered to employees because the employer merely distributes or posts education materials, sends them by electronic mail, or posts them on a bulletin board, the prevention education shall not be deemed provided.
  (4) Notwithstanding paragraphs (2) and (3), the employer of any business falling under any of the following subparagraphs may provide workplace sexual harassment prevention education by posting or distributing education materials or promotional materials so that employees may know the details under paragraph (2) 1 through 4: <Amended on Dec. 30, 2014>
  1. A business that employs fewer than 10 employees on a regular basis;
  2. A business in which both the employer and all employees are of only 1 gender, either male or female.
  (5) If an employer has employees complete a training course, among those recognized under Article 24 of the National Lifelong Vocational Skills Development Act, that contains the matters under each subparagraph of paragraph (2), the prevention education under paragraph (1) shall be deemed to have been provided to employees who have completed the relevant training course. <Amended on Feb. 17, 2022>

Article 4 (Businesses required to formulate and submit implementation plans for proactive employment improvement measures) (1) "Public institutions and organizations prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 17-3 (1) 1 of the Act means public institutions under Article 4 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions, local government-invested public corporations under Article 49 of the Local Public Enterprises Act, and local public agencies under Article 76 of that Act. <Amended on Dec. 19, 2017>
  (2) "Business employing no fewer than the number of employees prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 17-3 (1) 2 of the Act means any of the following businesses: <Amended on May 28, 2018; Dec. 28, 2021>
  1. In the case of a business of a business group subject to disclosure designated under Article 31 (1) of the Monopoly Regulation and Fair Trade Act and Article 38 (1) of the Enforcement Decree of that Act, a business that employs at least 300 employees on a regular basis;
  2. In the case of a business other than that under subparagraph 1, a business that employs at least 500 employees on a regular basis.
  (3) In applying paragraph (2), the number of employees employed on a regular basis shall be calculated by dividing the annual sum of the monthly average number of employees employed each month in the previous year by the number of months of operation in that year.

Article 5 (Institutions entrusted with evaluation of performance results) (1) “Institution or organization prescribed by Presidential Decree” in Article 17-4 (6) of the Act means a research institute established under Article 8 of the Act on the Establishment, Operation and Fostering of Government-Funded Research Institutes, or a research institute or corporation designated by the Minister of Gender Equality and Family from among non-profit corporations established under Article 32 of the Civil Act. <Amended on Jul. 12, 2010; Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) If the Minister of Gender Equality and Family entrusts the evaluation duties under Article 17-4 (6) of the Act, the Minister may provide the institution entrusted with the duties with expenses necessary for the performance of such duties. <Amended on Jul. 12, 2010; Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 6 (Grounds for exception to publication of list) (1) "Where any ground prescribed by Presidential Decree exists, such as the death of the employer and the dissolution of the enterprise" in the proviso of Article 17-5 (1) of the Act means any of the following:
  1. Where the employer has died;
  2. Where the workplace has undergone permanent closure of business or dissolution;
  3. Where it is impracticable to carry out an implementation plan under Article 17-3 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "implementation plan") due to serious managerial reasons, including being subject to a decision to commence rehabilitation procedures, or a declaration of bankruptcy under the Debtor Rehabilitation and Bankruptcy Act;
  4. Where an employer is making substantive efforts to carry out an implementation plan, including recruitment of female employees or appointment of female managers (referring to persons in charge of a unit department of a workplace who plan and direct the business of the relevant department and supervise and evaluate its members; hereinafter the same shall apply).
  (2) When the Minister of Gender Equality and Family determines whether an employer falls under any subparagraph of paragraph (1), they shall undergo deliberation by the Employment Policy Deliberative Council under subparagraph 5 of Article 17-8 of the Act. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  [This Article Added on Dec. 30, 2014]

Article 7 (Details and method of publication of list) (1) If the Minister of Gender Equality and Family intends to publish a list under the main clause of Article 17-5 (1) of the Act, the Minister shall notify an employer subject to such publication in writing of the determination to publish the list and the details thereof. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (2) The Minister of Gender Equality and Family shall give the employer an opportunity to submit explanatory materials or to state their opinions for a period of at least 30 days from the date the employer receives the notice under paragraph (1). <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (3) The details of publication under Article 17-5 (2) of the Act shall be as follows:
  1. The name of the relevant employer and the name and address of the workplace; in such cases, when the relevant employer is a corporation, this means the name of its representative and the name and address of the corporation;
  2. The total number of employees for the relevant year, the number of female employees and the ratio thereof, the total number of managers for the relevant year, the number of female managers and the ratio thereof, and the employment standards for female employees of the relevant type of business.
  (4) Publication under Article 17-5 (2) of the Act shall be made by publishing the list in the Official Gazette or posting it on the website of the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family for 6 months. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  [This Article Added on Dec. 30, 2014]

Article 8 Deleted. <Dec. 30, 2009>

Article 9 (Institutions entrusted with surveys and research) "Persons prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 17-9 (2) of the Act means research institutes established under Article 8 of the Act on the Establishment, Operation and Fostering of Government-Funded Research Institutes, or research institutes or corporations designated by the Minister of Gender Equality and Family from among non-profit corporations established under Article 32 of the Civil Act. <Amended on Jul. 12, 2010; Dec. 30, 2014; Oct. 1, 2025>

CHAPTER III MATERNITY PROTECTION AND WORK-FAMILY BALANCE ASSISTANCE

Article 9-2 (Application for fertility treatment leave) (1) An employee who intends to apply for leave to receive fertility treatment under Article 18-3 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "fertility treatment leave") shall submit to the employer a document (including electronic documents) stating the date on which they intend to use the fertility treatment leave, the date of application, etc. <Amended on Dec. 24, 2019>
  (2) An employer may require an employee who has applied for fertility treatment leave to submit a document evidencing that they will receive such fertility treatment.
  [This Article Added on May 28, 2018]

Article 10 (Exclusion from childcare leave) “ Cases prescribed by Presidential Decree” in the proviso of Article 19 (1) of the Act means cases where an employee whose period of continuous service in the relevant business is less than 6 months as of the day before the scheduled commencement date of childcare leave (hereinafter referred to as “scheduled commencement date of childcare leave”) files an application for childcare leave.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 24, 2019]

Article 11 (Application for childcare leave) (1) An employee who intends to apply for childcare leave under the main clause of Article 19 (1) of the Act shall submit to the employer, not later than 30 days before the scheduled commencement date of childcare leave, an application stating the following matters; in such cases, with respect to the matters under subparagraph 6, documents proving the relevant facts shall be attached to the application: <Amended on Nov. 19, 2021; Feb. 18, 2025>
  1. Personal information, such as the name and date of birth of the applicant;
  2. The name and the date of birth of an infant or young child for whom childcare leave is sought (where a pregnant female employee applies for childcare leave, the name of the infant or young child shall not be stated, and the expected date of delivery shall be stated in lieu of the date of birth);
  3. The scheduled commencement date of childcare leave;
  4. The date on which child care leave is to be terminated (hereinafter referred to as "scheduled termination date of childcare leave");
  5. The date of application for childcare leave;
  6. Where the employee falls under any subparagraph of Article 19 (2) of the Act, the fact that they fall under such subparagraph.
  (2) An employee who intends to commence childcare leave within 18 months after the birth of a child may apply for childcare leave in accordance with the main clause of Article 19 (1) of the Act when requesting maternity leave under Article 74 of the Labor Standards Act (hereinafter referred to as “maternity leave”) or when notifying paternity leave under Article 18-2 of the Act. In such cases, the employee shall submit to the employer, not later than 30 days before the scheduled commencement date of childcare leave, an application stating the matters under each subparagraph of paragraph (1) and the scheduled commencement and termination dates of maternity leave or paternity leave. <Added on Dec. 24, 2024; Feb. 18, 2025>
  (3) Notwithstanding the latter parts of paragraphs (1) and (2), an application for childcare leave may be filed not later than 7 days before the scheduled commencement date of childcare leave in any of the following cases: <Amended on Nov. 19, 2021; Dec. 24, 2024>
  1. Where a pregnant female employee is at risk of miscarriage or stillbirth;
  2. Where a child is born before the expected date of delivery;
  3. Where it is impracticable to rear the relevant infant or young child due to the death of the spouse, an injury, illness, physical or mental disability, divorce, etc.
  (4) If an employee applies for childcare leave under paragraphs (1) through (3), the employer shall allow the employee to take such leave. In such cases, the employer shall notify the employee in writing or by electronic means within 14 days from the date of application where the employee applies for childcare leave under paragraphs (1) and (2), and within 3 days from the date of application where the employee applies for childcare leave under paragraph (3). <Added on Dec. 24, 2024>
  (5) If an employer fails to notify an employee, within the period specified in the latter part of paragraph (4), that the employer allows the employee to take childcare leave, the employer shall be deemed to have allowed such childcare leave as applied for by the employee. <Added on Dec. 24, 2024>
  (6) If an employee applies for childcare leave after the deadline under paragraph (1) or the latter part of paragraph (2), the employer shall grant childcare leave by designating the commencement date of the leave within 30 days from the date of application, and if an employee applies for childcare leave after the deadline under paragraph (3), the employer shall grant childcare leave by designating the commencement date of the leave within 7 days from the date of application, and shall notify the employee of such fact in writing or by electronic means. <Amended on Dec. 24, 2024>
  (7) An employer may require an employee who applies for childcare leave under paragraphs (1) through (3) to submit documents proving the pregnancy of the employee or their spouse, or documents proving the birth of the child, etc. <Amended on Nov. 19, 2021; Dec. 24, 2024>

Article 12 (Application for change of childcare leave) (1) An employee who has applied for childcare leave may, if grounds falling under any subparagraph of Article 11 (3) arise before the scheduled commencement date of childcare leave, request the employer to change such date to a date earlier than the originally scheduled commencement date of childcare leave, stating such grounds. <Amended on Dec. 24, 2024>
  (2) If an employee intends to postpone the scheduled termination date of childcare leave, they may do so only once. In such cases, the employee shall file an application with the employer for postponement of the scheduled termination date of childcare leave not later than 30 days before the originally scheduled termination date of childcare leave (where the employee intends to postpone the scheduled termination date of childcare leave on the grounds falling under subparagraph 1 or 3 of Article 11 (3), not later than 7 days before the originally scheduled termination date of childcare leave). <Amended on Nov. 19, 2021; Dec. 24, 2024>

Article 13 (Withdrawal of application for childcare leave) (1) An employee who has applied for childcare leave may withdraw the relevant application, stating the grounds therefor, not later than 7 days prior to the scheduled commencement date of childcare leave.
  (2) If, after an employee applies for childcare leave and before the scheduled commencement date of childcare leave, any cause or event falling under the following subparagraphs occurs, the employee shall be deemed not to have filed the application for childcare leave: <Amended on Nov. 19, 2021; Feb. 18, 2025>
  1. Where a pregnant female employee applies for childcare leave: Miscarriage or stillbirth;
  2. Where an employee other than those referred to in subparagraph 1 applies for childcare leave:
  a. Where the relevant infant and young child dies;
  b. Where the adoption of the infant or young child is annulled or dissolved;
  c. Where the employee who has applied for childcare leave becomes unable to rear the relevant infant or young child due to an injury, illness, physical or mental disability, divorce, etc.;
  d. Where an employee who has applied for additional childcare leave of up to 6 months on the grounds under Article 19 (2) 2 or 3 of the Act no longer falls under such grounds.
  (3) If any cause or event under the subparagraphs of paragraph (2) occurs, the employee shall, without delay, notify the employer of such fact. <Added on Nov. 19, 2021>

Article 14 (End of childcare leave) (1) If any of the following events occur, an employee on childcare leave shall notify the employer of such fact within 7 days from the date of occurrence of the event: <Amended on Nov. 19, 2021>
  1. Where a pregnant female employee is on childcare leave: Miscarriage or stillbirth;
  2. Where an employee other than those referred to in subparagraph 1 is on childcare leave:
  a. Where the relevant infant and young child dies;
  b. Where the employee no longer lives with the relevant infant or young child and ceases to contribute to the rearing of the infant or young child.
  (2) Upon receipt of a notice under paragraph (1) relating to the death of the infant or young child, etc., the employer shall designate the date on which the employee is to return to work within 30 days from the date of receipt of the notice, and notify the employee of such date.
  (3) The childcare leave of an employee shall be deemed to end on any of the following dates:
  1. On the day immediately preceding the date on which the employee is to return to work, where the employee gives a notice under paragraph (1) and is notified of the date on which the employee is to return to work under paragraph (2);
  2. On the date when 30 days elapse from the date on which the employee gives a notice under paragraph (1), where the employee gives a notice under paragraph (1) but is not notified of the date on which the employee is to return to work under paragraph (2);
  3. On the date when 37 days elapse from the date of the occurrence of grounds such as the death of the infant or young child, where the employee fails to give a notice under paragraph (1).
  (4) If an employee on childcare leave begins new childcare leave, maternity leave, or reduced working hours during a period of childcare under Article 19-2 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as “reduced working hours during a period of childcare”), the childcare leave shall be deemed to end on the day immediately preceding the commencement date of the relevant new childcare leave, maternity leave, or reduced working hours during a period of childcare. <Amended on Jul. 10, 2012; Nov. 19, 2021; Dec. 24, 2024>
  [Title Amended on Dec. 24, 2019]

Article 15 (Application for reduced working hours during period of childcare) (1) An employee who intends to apply for reduced working hours during a period of childcare under the main clause of Article 19-2 (1) of the Act shall submit to the employer, not later than 30 days before the scheduled commencement date of such reduced working hours (hereinafter referred to as "scheduled commencement date of reduced working hours"), a document (including electronic documents) stating the name and date of birth of the child to be reared during the period of reduced working hours, the scheduled commencement date of reduced working hours, the date on which reduced working hours during a period of childcare is to be terminated (hereinafter referred to as "scheduled termination date of reduced working hours"), the time to start and the time to end work during the period of reduced working hours, the date of application, the particulars of the applicant, etc.
  (2) If an employee applies for reduced working hours during a period of childcare after the deadline under paragraph (1), the employer shall allow the employee to work under reduced working hours during a period of childcare by designating the commencement date thereof within 30 days from the date of application.
  (3) An employer may require an employee who applies for reduced working hours during a period of childcare under paragraph (1) or (2) to submit documents proving the birth of the relevant child, etc.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 10, 2012]
  [Previous Article 15 moved to Article 15-4 <Jul 10, 2012>]

Article 15-2 (Exceptions to allowing reduced working hours during period of childcare) "Cases prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the proviso of Article 19-2 (1) of the Act means any of the following cases: <Amended on Dec. 24, 2019>
  1. Where an employee whose period of continuous service in the relevant business is less than 6 months as of the day before the scheduled commencement date of reduced working hours applies for such reduced working hours;
  2. Deleted; <Dec. 24, 2019>
  3. Where an employer, after filing a job application with an employment security office defined in subparagraph 1 of Article 2-2 of the Employment Security Act (hereinafter referred to as "employment security office") and endeavoring for at least 14 days to recruit replacement personnel, fails to employ such replacement personnel; provided, this shall not apply where the employer has rejected employment on at least 2 occasions without good cause despite job placement services provided by the head of the employment security office;
  4. Where, given the nature of the duties of the employee who applies for reduced working hours during a period of childcare, it is impracticable to divide the working hours, or where such reduced working hours substantially impede the normal operation of the business, and the employer proves such circumstance.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 10, 2012]

Article 15-3 (End of reduced working hours during period of childcare) (1) An employee on reduced working hours during a period of childcare shall, where the relevant infant or young child dies or the employee no longer lives with the infant or young child (limited to where the employee ceases to contribute to the rearing of the infant or young child), notify the employer of such fact within 7 days from the date of occurrence of the cause. <Amended on Dec. 24, 2019>
  (2) Upon receipt of a notice under paragraph (1) relating to the death, etc. of the infant or young child, the employer shall designate the date on which the employee is to return to their previous duties, within 30 days from the date of receipt of the notice, and notify the employee of such date.
  (3) The reduced working hours during a period of childcare of an employee shall be deemed to end on any of the following dates:
  1. On the day immediately preceding the date on which the employee is to return to their previous duties, where the employee gives a notice under paragraph (1) and is notified of the date on which the employee is to return to such duties under paragraph (2);
  2. On the date when 30 days elapse from the date on which the employee gives a notice under paragraph (1), where the employee gives a notice under paragraph (1) but is not notified of the date on which the employee is to return to their previous duties under paragraph (2);
  3. On the date when 37 days elapse from the date of occurrence of a ground for ending the reduced working hours during a period of childcare, such as the death of the infant or young child, where the employee fails to give a notice under paragraph (1).
  (4) If an employee on reduced working hours during a period of childcare falls under any of the following cases, the reduced working hours during a period of childcare shall be deemed to end on the day immediately preceding the dates classified as follows: <Amended on Dec. 24, 2024>
  1. Where the employee starts using new reduced working hours during a period of childcare: The commencement date of the new reduced working hours during a period of childcare;
  2. Where the employee begins childcare leave or maternity leave: The commencement date of such childcare leave or maternity leave;
  3. Where the employee begins a leave of absence or time off (limited to one that continues for at least 30 days) for any reason other than those referred to in subparagraph 2: The commencement date of such leave of absence or time off;
  4. Where temporary closure of business (limited to one that continues for at least 30 days) begins due to a cause attributable to the employer: The commencement date of such temporary closure of business.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 10, 2012]
  [Title Amended on Dec. 24, 2019]

Article 15-4 (Application mutatis mutandis) The provisions of Articles 12 (2) and 13 shall apply mutatis mutandis to procedures for reduced working hours during a period of childcare under Article 19-2 of the Act. In such cases, "childcare leave" shall be construed as "reduced working hours during a period of childcare"; "scheduled commencement date of childcare leave" as "scheduled commencement date of reduced working hours"; and "scheduled termination date of childcare leave" as "scheduled termination date of reduced working hours".
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jul. 10, 2012]
  [Moved from Article 15 <Jul. 10, 2012>]

Article 16 (Areas for preferential installation of welfare facilities) If the State or a local government installs public welfare facilities for female employees under Article 22 (1) of the Act, it shall give priority to installing such facilities in areas where female employees are concentrated, such as industrial complexes or agro-industrial zones.

Article 16-2 (Application for family care leave and short-term family care leave) (1) An employee who intends to apply for family care leave under the main clause of Article 22-2 (1) of the Act shall submit to the employer, not later than 30 days before the scheduled commencement date of family care leave (hereinafter referred to as "scheduled commencement date of family care leave"), a document (including electronic documents) stating the name and date of birth of the family member to be cared for during the period of family care leave, the grounds for care, the scheduled commencement date of family care leave, the date on which the family care leave is to be terminated (hereinafter referred to as "scheduled termination date of family care leave"), the date of application for family care leave, the particulars of the applicant, etc.
  (2) If an employee applies for family care leave after the deadline under paragraph (1), the employer shall allow the employee to take such leave by designating the commencement date of the family care leave within 30 days from the date of application.
  (3) An employer may require an employee who has applied for family care leave to submit documents proving the necessity of the employee’s family care leave, such as documents showing the health condition of the family member in need of care or whether another family member, other than the applicant, is able to provide such care.
  (4) An employee who intends to apply for short-term family care leave under the main clause of Article 22-2 (2) of the Act shall submit to the employer a document (including electronic documents) stating the date on which the short-term family care leave is to be used, the name and date of birth of the family member to be cared for during the short-term family care leave, the date of application for short-term family care leave, the particulars of the applicant, etc. <Added on Dec. 24, 2019>
  [This Article Added on Jul. 10, 2012]
  [Title Amended on Dec. 24, 2019]

Article 16-3 (Exceptions to allowing family care leave and short-term family care leave) (1) "Cases prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the proviso of Article 22-2 (1) of the Act means any of the following cases: <Amended on Dec. 24, 2019>
  1. Where an employee whose period of continuous service in the relevant business is less than 6 months as of the day before the scheduled commencement date of family care leave applies for such leave;
  2. Where any parent, child, spouse, or other family member of the family member in need of care, other than the employee who applies for family care leave to care for their parent, spouse, child, or the parent of their spouse, is able to provide such care;
  3. Where the grandparents or grandchildren of the employee who applies for family care leave have their lineal descendant or lineal ascendant, other than the employee; provided, this shall not apply where the employee shall take care of their grandparents or grandchildren because such lineal descendant or lineal ascendant is sick, old, disabled, or a minor, etc.;
  4. Where an employer fails to employ replacement personnel despite their endeavor for at least 14 days to employ such personnel after filing a job application with an employment security office; provided, this shall not apply where the employer has rejected employment on at least 2 occasions without good cause despite job placement services provided by the head of the employment security office;
  5. Where an employee's family care leave substantially impedes the normal operation of the business, and the employer proves such fact.
  (2) “Cases prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as where grandparents or grandchildren have other lineal descendants or lineal ascendants in addition to the employee” in the main clause of Article 22-2 (2) of the Act means where the grandparents or grandchildren, other than the employee who applies for short-term family care leave to take care of them, have their lineal descendant or lineal ascendant; provided, this shall not apply where the employee shall take care of their grandparents or grandchildren because such lineal descendant or lineal ascendant is sick, elderly, disabled, or a minor, etc. <Added on Dec. 24, 2019>
  [This Article Added on Jul. 10, 2012]
  [Title Amended on Dec. 24, 2019]

Article 16-4 (Withdrawal of application for family care leave) (1) An employee who applies for family care leave may withdraw the application, clarifying the grounds therefor, not later than 7 days prior to the scheduled commencement date of family care leave.
  (2) If an employee applies for family care leave, but the family member in need of care dies or recovers from a disease, etc. before the scheduled commencement date of family care leave, the application shall be deemed not filed. In such cases, the employee shall notify the employer of such fact without delay.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 24, 2019]
  [Previous Article 16-4 moved to Article 16-6 <Dec. 24, 2019>]

Article 16-5 (End of family care leave) (1) If a family member in need of care is dead or recovers from a disease, etc., an employee on family care leave shall notify their employer of such fact within 7 days from the date of the occurrence of such ground.
  (2) If an employer is notified under paragraph (1), they shall designate the date on which the employee is to return to work within 30 days from the date of receipt of the notice and notify the employee of such date.
  (3) Family care leave shall be deemed to end on any of the following dates:
  1. On the day immediately preceding the date on which the employee is to return to work, where the employee gives a notice under paragraph (1) and is notified of the date on which the employee is to return to work under paragraph (2);
  2. On the date when 30 days elapse from the date on which the employee gives a notice under paragraph (1), where the employee gives a notice under paragraph (1) but is not notified of the date on which the employee is to return to work under paragraph (2);
  3. On the date when 37 days elapse from the date of occurrence of the grounds under paragraph (1), where the employee fails to give a notice under paragraph (1).
  [This Article Added on Dec. 24, 2019]

Article 16-6 (Application mutatis mutandis) The provisions of Article 12 (2) shall apply mutatis mutandis to procedures, etc. for a family care leave under Article 22-2 (1) of the Act. In such cases, "scheduled termination date of childcare leave" shall be construed as "scheduled termination date of family care leave". <Amended on Dec. 24, 2019>
  [This Article Added on Jul. 10, 2012]
  [Moved from Article 16-4 <Dec. 24, 2019>]

Article 16-7 (Application for reduced working hours for family care, etc.) (1) An employee who intends to apply for reduced working hours for family care, etc. under Article 22-3 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as “reduced working hours for family care, etc.”) shall submit to their employer, not later than 30 days before the date on which the employee is to start reduced working hours for family care, etc. (hereinafter referred to as the “scheduled commencement date of reduced working hours for family care, etc.”), a document (including electronic documents) stating the grounds for such application, the scheduled commencement date of reduced working hours for family care, etc., the date on which the employee is to end reduced working hours for family care, etc. (hereinafter referred to as the “scheduled termination date of reduced working hours for family care, etc.”), the work start and end times during the period of reduced working hours for family care, etc., the application date, the particulars of the applicant, etc.
  (2) If an employee applies for reduced working hours for family care, etc. after the deadline under paragraph (1), the employer shall allow the employee to work under reduced working hours for family care, etc. by designating the commencement date of reduced working hours for family care, etc. within 30 days from the date of the application, and shall notify the employee of such date.    
  (3) If an employee who applies for reduced working hours for family care, etc. under paragraphs (1) and (2) is not notified by the employer, within 30 days from the date of the application, that the employer allows the employee to work under reduced working hours for family care, etc., it shall be deemed that the employer has allowed the employee to work under reduced working hours for family care, etc. as applied for by the employee.
  (4) An employer may require an employee who applies for reduced working hours for family care, etc. under paragraphs (1) and (2) to submit documents proving the relevant grounds, such as a family member's disease.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 24, 2019]

Article 16-8 (Exceptions to approval of reduced working hours for family care, etc.) "Cases prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as where it is impossible to hire substitute personnel or where the normal operation of the business would be significantly impeded" in the proviso, with the exception of the subparagraphs, of Article 22-3 (1) of the Act means any of the following cases:
  1. Where an employee whose period of continuous service in the relevant business is less than 6 months as of the day before the scheduled commencement date of the reduced working hours for family care, etc. applies for such reduced working hours;
  2. Where an employer, after filing a job application with an employment security office and endeavoring for at least 14 days to recruit substitute personnel, fails to employ such personnel; provided, this shall not apply where the employer has rejected employment on at least 2 occasions without good cause despite job placement services provided by the head of the employment security office;
  3. Where, given the nature of the duties of the employee who applies for reduced working hours for family care, etc., it is impracticable to divide the working hours or where such reduced working hours for family care, etc. substantially impede the normal operation of the business, and the employer proves such fact;
  4. Where an employee applies for reduced working hours for family care, etc. before 2 years have elapsed since the termination date of the previous reduced working hours for family care, etc.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 24, 2019]

Article 16-9 (Application for extension of period of reduced working hours for family care, etc.) (1) An employee who intends to apply for an extension of the period of reduced working hours for family care, etc. shall submit to the employer, not later than 30 days before the scheduled termination date of the reduced working hours for family care, etc., a document (including electronic documents) stating the grounds for the extension, the originally scheduled termination date of the reduced working hours for family care, etc., the scheduled termination date of the reduced working hours for family care, etc. following the extension, the work start time and work end time during the extended period of the reduced working hours for family care, etc., the date of the application for the extension of the period of reduced working hours for family care, etc., the particulars of the applicant, etc.
  (2) If an employee applies for an extension of the period of reduced working hours for family care, etc. after the deadline under paragraph (1), the employer shall designate the extended period of such reduced working hours within 30 days from the date of the application and allow the employee to work under reduced working hours for family care, etc.
  (3) The extension of the period under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be limited to 1 occasion.
  (4) If an employee applies for an extension of the period of reduced working hours for family care, etc. under paragraphs (1) and (2) but is not notified by the employer that the employer allows the employee to work under extended period of reduced working hours for family care, etc. within 30 days from the date of the application, it shall be deemed that the employer has allowed such extended period of reduced working hours for family care, etc. as applied for by the employee.
  (5) An employer may require an employee who applies for an extension of the period of reduced working hours for family care, etc. under paragraphs (1) and (2) to submit documents proving the relevant grounds, such as a family member's disease.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 24, 2019]

Article 16-10 (Withdrawal of application for reduced working hours for family care, etc.) (1) An employee who files an application for reduced working hours for family care, etc. may withdraw such application not later than 7 days prior to the scheduled commencement date of the reduced working hours for family care, etc., explaining the grounds therefor.
  (2) If any of the grounds classified in the following subparagraphs occurs before the scheduled commencement date of the reduced working hours for family care, etc. after an employee files an application for reduced working hours for family care, etc., the application shall be deemed not filed. In such cases, the employee shall notify the employer of such fact without delay:
  1. Where an application is filed on the grounds under Article 22-3 (1) 1 of the Act: The death of the relevant family member or the recovery from their illness, etc.;
  2. Where an application is filed on the grounds under Article 22-3 (1) 2 of the Act: The recovery from the relevant illness, injury, etc.;
  3. Where an application is filed on the grounds under Article 22-3 (1) 3 or 4 of the Act: The revocation of preparations for retirement or study plans due to changed circumstances.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 24, 2019]

Article 16-11 (End of reduced working hours for family care, etc.) (1) If any of the grounds classified as follows occur, an employee on reduced working hours for family care, etc. shall notify their employer of such fact within 7 days from the date of the occurrence of the ground:
  1. Where the employee is on reduced working hours for family care, etc. on the grounds under Article 22-3 (1) 1 of the Act: The relevant family member's death or the recovery from their illness, etc.;
  2. Where the employee is on reduced working hours for family care, etc. on the grounds under Article 22-3 (1) 2 of the Act: The recovery from the relevant illness, injury, etc.;
  3. Where the employee is on reduced working hours for family care, etc. on the grounds under Article 22-3 (1) 3 or 4 of the Act: The suspension of preparations for retirement or study due to changed circumstances.
  (2) If an employer is notified under paragraph (1), they shall designate a date on which the employee is to return to their previous duties and notify the employee thereof within 30 days from the date they are notified.
  (3) The reduced working hours for family care, etc. of an employee shall be deemed to end on any of the following dates:
  1. On the day preceding the date on which the employee is to return to their previous duties, where the employee gives a notice under paragraph (1) and is notified under paragraph (2) of the date on which the employee is to return to their previous duties;
  2. On the date when 30 days elapse from the date of giving a notice under paragraph (1), where an employee gives a notice under paragraph (1) but is not notified of the date on which the employee is to return to their previous duties under paragraph (2);
  3. On the date when 37 days elapse from the date of the occurrence of the grounds classified under each subparagraph of paragraph (1), where an employee fails to give a notice under paragraph (1).
  [This Article Added on Dec. 24, 2019]

Article 17 (Entrustment of duties, such as surveys and research for work-family balance assistance) Under Article 22-5 (2) of the Act, the Minister of Employment and Labor may entrust the duties relating to support for the establishment and operation of workplace child care centers under Articles 21 and 21-2 of the Act, and the duties relating to the establishment of a foundation for work-family balance assistance under Article 22-5 (1) of the Act, to any of the following institutions or corporations:
  1. A quasi-governmental institution under Article 5 (4) 2 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions;
  2. A research institute under Article 8 of the Act on the Establishment, Operation and Fostering of Government-Funded Research Institutes;
  3. A non-profit corporation under Article 32 of the Civil Act, whose purpose is to implement businesses relating to work-family balance assistance, etc.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 24, 2024]

CHAPTER IV PREVENTION AND SETTLEMENT OF DISPUTES

Article 18 (Reporting of grievances) (1) A report on grievances under Article 25 of the Act shall be filed verbally, in writing, by mail, by telephone or fax, or via the Internet, etc.
  (2) Upon receipt of a report on a grievance under paragraph (1), the employer shall handle the grievance directly within 10 days from the date of receipt or entrust the handling to the labor-management council established under the Act on the Promotion of Employees' Participation and Cooperation, unless there is a compelling reason not to do so. In such cases, the employer shall notify the relevant employee of the results if the grievance is handled directly, or inform the employee of the entrustment if the handling is entrusted to the labor-management council.
  (3) Each employer shall prepare and keep a ledger for the acceptance and handling of grievances, and shall retain the relevant documents for 3 years.
  (4) The ledger for the acceptance and handling of grievances under paragraph (3) shall be prepared and kept by means enabling electronic processing, unless there is a compelling reason that makes such electronic processing impracticable, and the documents under that paragraph may be prepared and retained by electronic means.

Article 18-2 (Number of and qualification requirements for expert members) (1) Expert members under Article 27 (5) of the Act shall be assigned to the National Labor Relations Commission or Regional Labor Relations Commissions under Article 2 (1) of the Labor Relations Commission Act.
  (2) The number of expert members assigned to the National Labor Relations Commission or Regional Labor Relations Commissions under Article 2 (1) of the Labor Relations Commission Act under paragraph (1) shall not exceed 10 persons.
  (3) Expert members under paragraph (2) shall be persons commissioned by the chairperson of the National Labor Relations Commission established under Article 2 (1) of the Labor Relations Commission Act (hereinafter referred to as the “National Labor Relations Commission”) from among the following persons:
  1. A person holding a doctoral degree in a field related to employment and labor, such as law, business administration, economics, sociology, or women’s studies;
  2. A person qualified as an attorney-at-law, certified public accountant, or certified public labor attorney.
  (4) Matters relating to the remuneration of expert members under paragraph (2) shall be separately determined by the National Labor Relations Commission, by applying mutatis mutandis the standard table of salary grades of fixed-term public officials in general service as specified in Appendix 34 of the Public Officials Remuneration Regulations.
  [This Article Added on Nov. 19, 2021]

CHAPTER V SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 19 (Types of retained documents) "Documents prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 33 of the Act means the following: <Amended on May 28, 2018; Feb. 18, 2025>
  1. Documents relating to recruitment and employment, wages, money or goods other than wages, education, assignment, promotion, retirement age, retirement, and dismissal under Articles 7 through 11 of the Act;
  2. Documents verifying that workplace sexual harassment prevention education under Articles 13 and 13-2 of the Act has been provided;
  3. Documents relating to measures, such as disciplinary action, taken against a workplace sexual harassment offender under the former part of Article 14 (5) of the Act;
  4. Deleted; <Jun. 19, 2009>
  5. Documents relating to the notification and approval of paternity leave under Article 18-2 of the Act;
  6. Documents relating to applications for, and the approval of, childcare leave under Article 19 of the Act;
  7. Documents relating to applications for, and approval of, reduced working hours during a period of childcare under Articles 19-2 and 19-3 of the Act, documents relating to notifications of the grounds for refusal and consultations where such applications are not allowed, and documents relating to working conditions during the period of reduced working hours during a period of childcare.

Article 20 Deleted. <Dec. 30, 2014>

Article 21 (Delegation and entrustment of authority) (1) Under Article 36 of the Act, the Minister of Employment and Labor shall delegate the following authority to the heads of regional employment and labor offices: <Amended on Jul. 12, 2010; Dec. 8, 2011; Mar. 8, 2016>
  1. Authority relating to the designation of, and revocation of designation of, institutions for sexual harassment prevention education under Article 13-2 of the Act;
  2. Authority relating to subsidizing expenses for the establishment or operation of facilities for promoting the employment of women and for implementing such businesses under Article 17 of the Act;
  3. Deleted; <Oct. 1, 2025>
  4. Deleted; <Oct. 1, 2025>
  5. Authority relating to providing assistance, guidance, information, and counseling necessary for the establishment and operation of workplace child care centers under Articles 21 (3) and 21-2 of the Act;
  6. Authority relating to subsidizing expenses incurred by private organizations that provide counseling services under Article 23 of the Act;
  7. Authority relating to the commissioning and decommissioning of honorary supervisors for equal employment under Article 24 of the Act;
  8. Authority relating to issuing orders to submit reports and relevant documents, entering workplaces, making inquiries of relevant persons, and inspecting relevant documents under Article 31 of the Act;
  9. Authority relating to the imposition and collection of administrative fines under Article 39 of the Act.
  (2) Under Article 36 of the Act, the Minister of Employment and Labor may entrust fact-finding surveys under Article 6-3 of the Act to any of the following public organizations: <Added on Dec. 12, 2023>
  1. A public institution under Article 4 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions;
  2. A government-funded research institute established under Article 8 of the Act on the Establishment, Operation and Fostering of Government-Funded Research Institutes;
  3. Other public organizations that the Minister of Employment and Labor recognizes as having the human resources, facilities, and equipment necessary to perform the entrusted duties.
  (3) Under Article 36 of the Act, the Minister of Employment and Labor shall entrust the following duties to the Korea Employment Information Service under Article 18 of the Framework Act on Employment Policy: <Added on Mar. 8, 2016; Nov. 19, 2021; Dec. 12, 2023>
  1. Requests for the provision of materials relating to applications for benefits to cover medical expenses for pregnancy and childbirth under Article 31-2 (1) of the Act;
  2. Processing of provided materials through the employment information system under Article 31-2 (2) of the Act.
  (4) If the Minister of Employment and Labor entrusts duties under paragraph (2), they shall publicly notify the public organization entrusted with such duties and the details of the entrusted duties. <Added on Dec. 12, 2023>
  [Title Amended on March 8, 2016]

Article 21-2 (Processing of sensitive information and personally identifiable information) The Minister of Employment and Labor (including persons to whom the Minister’s authority is delegated or entrusted under Article 21) may, if unavoidable to perform the following affairs, process data containing information on health under Article 23 of the Personal Information Protection Act, or materials containing resident registration numbers or alien registration numbers under subparagraph 1 or 4 of Article 19 of the Enforcement Decree of that Act: <Amended on Dec. 24, 2024>
  1. Affairs relating to providing guidance on the support system for maternity leave, etc. under Article 18 of the Act, and the support and guidance necessary for implementing such system;
  2. Affairs relating to providing guidance on the childcare leave system under Article 19 of the Act, and the support and guidance necessary for implementing such system;
  3. Affairs relating to providing guidance on the system of reduced working hours during a period of childcare under Articles 19-2 and 19-3 of the Act, and the support and guidance necessary for implementing such system;
  4. Affairs relating to the issuance of orders, entry, making inquiries, and inspecting relevant documents under Article 31 of the Act;
  5. Affairs relating to requests for the provision of materials under Article 31-2 of the Act and the processing of such materials through the employment insurance network.
  [This Article Added on Mar. 8, 2016]
  [Previous Article 21-2 moved to Article 21-3 <Mar. 8, 2016>]

Article 21-3 (Re-examination of regulation) The Minister of Employment and Labor shall examine the appropriateness of the types of retained documents under Article 19 every 5 years, counting from January 1, 2020 (referring to the period that ends on the day before January 1 of every fifth year) and shall take measures, such as making improvements. <Amended on Dec. 30, 2016; Mar. 3, 2020>
  [This Article Added on Dec. 9, 2014]
  [Moved from Article 21-2 <Mar. 8, 2016>]

CHAPTER VI ADMINISTRATIVE FINES

Article 22 (Criteria for imposition of administrative fines) (1) Criteria for the imposition of administrative fines under Article 39 (1) through (4) of the Act shall be as specified in the Appendix. <Amended on Nov. 19, 2021>
  (2) Deleted. <May 28, 2018>

Article 1 (Enforcement date)
This Decree shall enter into force on June 22, 2008; provided, the amended provisions of subparagraphs 4 through 6 of the Appendix shall enter into force on June 22, 2009.
Article 2 (Special cases concerning obligation to formulate and submit implementation plans for proactive employment improvement measures)
The amended provisions of Article 4 (1) shall not apply to public institutions with a regular workforce of fewer than 50 employees among the public institutions under Article 4 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions until April 30, 2013.

1. 2. Submission of a report on the current status of male and female employees by occupational category and position to be first submitted under Article 17-3 (2) of the Act: Year 2009;
3. Submission of performance results of implementation plans for proactive employment improvement measures to be first submitted under Article 17-4 (1) of the Act (limited to public institutions whose ratio of female employees by occupational category falls short of the employment standards under Article 17-3 (1) of the Act): Year 2010;

Article 5 (Relationship to other statutes or regulations)
If the previous Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Equal Employment for Both Sexes or any provision thereof is cited in other statutes or regulations as at the time this Decree enters into force, if any corresponding provision thereto exists in this Decree, this Decree or the corresponding provisions herein shall be deemed cited in lieu of the previous provisions.
